tasks.design: Configure existing encounter-to-grouper input mapping in {OTHER}, the clinical registry and approved DRG software. Keep exception resolution and final assignment review with the registrar; existing grouper calculation runtime earns no new saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some coded encounter fields may still require manual transfer into the grouping worklist.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mapping can remove supported input transfer without replacing the established grouping rules.
tasks.still_hard: Identify incomplete or contradictory encounter inputs.
tasks.human_edge: Accept a traceable assignment based on verified records.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: DRG assignment uses rule-based grouping software with coded encounter inputs.

assumptions: Preserve the stated DRG task; do not substitute a Dutch reimbursement scheme. Coding/abstraction is existing prerequisite work, not removed from this task.

Existing coding staff supply encounter ID, diagnosis/procedure codes, dates and required patient/discharge attributes under the approved grouper specification. Mapping reads existing fields; s2 resolves missing values manually with source owners. No new code or patient attribute is inferred.

Native mapping is tried first. Central requires real current manual transfer and supported fields for half that effort; if fully integrated already, no saving. s3 includes only human software operation, not automatic grouper runtime.
Same-encounter save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Final assignment precedes approval and edits invalidate it.
Provisional B=100, R=87.5, gross=12.5; focal upkeep=0.5; net=12. Shares are independent of means priors.

steps.what: Define the report population, period and disease, surgery or bed-use measures
Extract and combine the medical care and census data for the defined report

steps.what: Reconcile duplicate encounters, missing classifications and census-period boundaries
Compile disease, surgery and bed-use tables into the statistical report
outputs: medical care and census report draft v1

inputs: medical care and census report draft v1
outputs: approved care and census report v1

steps.what: Save the approved statistical report in its current report record
inputs: approved care and census report v1
outputs: saved care and census report v1

tasks.design: Configure extracts from {OTHER}, the patient administration system, into {DATA_PLATFORM} and native {BI} report tables. The technologist reconciles source issues and approves the final {DOCS} report; no external delivery is included.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compilation can require repeated extraction and table assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned deterministic queries and native report definitions can repeat the supported compilation.
tasks.still_hard: Define and reconcile census boundaries and incomplete classifications.
tasks.human_edge: Accept data quality, definitions and appropriate disclosure.

ambition.what: Refresh consistent care and census statistics more often.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: encounter and bed-movement records can support deterministic statistical extracts and reports.

assumptions: Boundary is compiling the statistical report, including reconciliation and review; source clinical coding and external submission are separate work.

Existing clinical and administrative staff record encounter ID, disease/procedure codes and dates, admission/discharge, ward/bed movement times and statuses. s1 confirms population, period, measure definitions and suppression scope. Missing data returns to normal source enquiry in s3; no new upstream capture is assumed.

Native extracts and reports come first. Central retains 25% of extraction/combination and 30% of report assembly effort; reconciliation and final review remain fully counted. Query runtime is not human baseline.
Same-record save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Approval follows final report creation and edits void it.
Provisional B=100, R=59.75, gross=40.25; focal upkeep=1.25; net=39, independent of means priors.

tasks.short: Design secure and reliable healthcare databases

steps.what: Elicit healthcare application data requirements and workload constraints
outputs: recorded database requirements and workload cases

steps.what: Define data protection boundaries, access roles and reliability requirements
inputs: recorded database requirements and workload cases
existing organisational security and recovery standards
outputs: approved design constraints and access model

steps.what: Draft the database schema, constraints and query/index design
inputs: recorded database requirements and workload cases
approved design constraints and access model

loop.purpose: Draft a schema and query/index proposal from stated requirements
loop.input: Requirements, access model, recovery constraints and existing schema conventions
loop.output: Reviewable schema design and rationale in an isolated workspace
loop.check: Technologist checks entity meaning, keys, temporal history, permissions, query behavior and recovery implications; tests invalid as well as valid cases
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved requirements return to manual design
loop.why_not_simpler: Mapping narrative healthcare workflows to entities and constraints requires interpretation; standard schema scaffolds are used first

steps.what: Test the design for access isolation, workload performance and recovery reliability
inputs: recorded database requirements and workload cases
approved design constraints and access model
outputs: tested design revisions and unresolved risks

steps.what: Document and approve the final database design and its limitations
inputs: tested design revisions and unresolved risks
approved design constraints and access model

steps.what: Save the approved design in the current design repository

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting assistant in {DATA_PLATFORM} to propose schema and query structures from recorded requirements. The technologist defines security and reliability constraints, tests the design in isolation and approves the final {DOCS} design; production deployment is separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schema drafting must translate varied workflow requirements into consistent structures.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded assistant can draft reviewable designs from explicit requirements and conventions.
tasks.still_hard: Guarantee clinical data meaning, access isolation and recovery behavior.
tasks.human_edge: Set architecture constraints and accept tested design trade-offs.

ambition.what: Reduce first-draft design work while retaining full testing.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded code assistants can draft schemas from requirements, but security and semantic correctness require independent tests.

assumptions: Boundary is database design, not production implementation or migration. Isolated tests use synthetic cases, not unapproved patient data.

s1 counts capture of entities, relationships, temporal history, query cases and load expectations; s2 counts access, recovery and retention constraints from current organisational standards. Missing requirements return to people, not model guesses.

Native schema scaffolds and deterministic checks come first. Central reduces drafting by 40% only; requirements, threat assessment, tests and final documentation remain unchanged. Test runtime is excluded from human baseline.
Same-repository save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Approval follows tested final revisions and changes void it.
Provisional B=100, R=90, gross=10; focal upkeep=1; net=9, independent of means priors.
unknowns: Coverage of workload and access tests
research_questions: Compare accepted designs and test failures with human-only drafts, including temporal and access-boundary errors.

already_counted.description: Independently test security, performance and reliability of the design

incremental.description: Maintain assistant constraints and audit recurring design errors

tasks.short: Develop healthcare information in-service learning materials

steps.what: Define staff learning needs and the healthcare information procedures to teach
outputs: learning objectives and chosen procedure scope

steps.what: Retrieve the current approved procedures, screens and example cases
inputs: learning objectives and chosen procedure scope
existing approved procedures and training examples

steps.what: Draft in-service explanations, exercises and answer guidance from the verified sources
inputs: learning objectives and chosen procedure scope

loop.purpose: Draft learning explanations and exercises for the selected procedures
loop.input: Approved procedure actions, screen references, synthetic cases and learning objectives
loop.output: Source-linked explanations, exercises and answer guidance
loop.check: Technologist executes each described action in a test system and checks exercise answers, permissions and teaching intent
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual completion of unresolved sections
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations and exercises must adapt procedure prose to staff learning needs; source lists and screenshots alone do not teach the workflow

steps.what: Try the exercises, revise unclear instructions and approve the final materials
Save the approved materials in the current training workspace

tasks.design: Link current {DOCS} procedures to bounded drafting of in-service materials, using {LMS} objectives. The technologist verifies all procedure actions and exercises in {OTHER}, the test healthcare application, before approving the final materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning approved procedures into teachable explanations and exercises takes composition work.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can assist explanations and exercise variations.
tasks.still_hard: Ensure the materials teach the actual permitted workflow.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize learner misunderstandings and validate procedure meaning.

ambition.what: Adapt verified materials for different staff learning needs.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-bound drafting can adapt procedure explanations and exercises with human execution checks.

assumptions: Boundary is developing materials, not delivering training or publishing to learners. No training-delivery savings are counted.

Existing procedure owners maintain version, intended role, prerequisites, exact action sequence, expected results, exceptions and screen references. s1 captures learning objectives. s2 checks source currency; missing actions require owner clarification before drafting. Use existing synthetic examples, not patient records.
Native source retrieval and course templates come first. Central reduces source retrieval by 25% and composition by 60%; full execution checks, revision and approval remain at 100%.
Same-workspace save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Approval follows final material revision and any edit voids it.
Provisional B=100, R=72.25, gross=27.75; focal upkeep=1.75; net=26, independent of means priors.
